content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey cacciatore is an Italian‑style dish made with bite‑size pieces of poultry simmered with tomatoes, bell pepper, onion, garlic, olives and aromatic herbs. Slow cooking in its own juices keeps the meat tender while the sauce develops a rich, slightly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “cacciatore” means “hunter” in Italian, originally referring to dishes made with game meat.
Traditional recipes used wild birds, but today chicken or turkey are the most common substitutes.
The dish is often served over polenta, pasta, or crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Tomatoes can be fresh or canned, making the recipe usable year‑round.
Some regional variations add red wine for extra depth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Low in saturated fat (especially turkey)
items.content: Skinless poultry contains little saturated fat, supporting heart‑healthy eating patterns.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies vitamin B6 and niacin, which aid metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants from tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may protect cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Minerals from olives and peppers
items.content: Olives and bell peppers add potassium, iron and magnesium, important for muscle and nerve health.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared tomato sauces or broths can be high in salt; choose low‑sodium versions when possible.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Poultry must reach a safe internal temperature to prevent salmonella.

items.title: Olives and additives
items.content: Cured olives add extra salt; rinse them if you need to reduce sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sear the chicken or turkey pieces until golden, then add onion, garlic, and bell pepper and sauté until softened. Stir in crushed tomatoes (or canned diced tomatoes), olives, herbs (oregano, basil), and a splash of wine if desired. Cover and simmer 30‑40 minutes until the meat is fully cooked and tender. Serve over pasta, polenta, or with crusty bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
